items.caption_intent: Figure 1, Wittauer et al., Orthopaedic Surgery 2026;18:2247-2259; DOI 10.1111/os.70426; supplied PDF page 2. The skin incision is made parallel to the iliac crest 1–2 cm distal to the ASIS (dotted line) (A). The ASIS osteotomy with the insertion of sartorius and the inguinal ligament is retracted medially, and a gauze pack is placed in the iliac fossa subperiosteally (B). Gl Mx, gluteus maximus; I, iliacus; PS, psoas; RF, rectus femoris; S, sartorius; TFL, tensor fasciae latae.

items.teaching_point_placement: Deep corridor to the ischium beside capsule and iliopsoas
items.caption_intent: Figure 4, Wittauer et al., Orthopaedic Surgery 2026;18:2247-2259; DOI 10.1111/os.70426; supplied PDF page 3. Illustration of the passage of the angled osteotome for the second osteotomy, the partial cut of the anterior ischium (2) after completion of the pubic ramus osteotomy (1). The osteotome is posi - tioned within the interval between the anterior column posteriorly, the iliocapsularis and joint capsule laterally, and the psoas medially. The dotted line represents the starting point of the second osteotome. Note that the osteotome position depicted in this illustration does not indicate the initial direction of advancement; the osteotomy trajectory should be oriented away from the sciatic nerve. IC, iliocapsularis; OEx, obturator externus; Ps, psoas; S, sartorius.

items.teaching_point_placement: Ischial osteotomy in AP and oblique fluoroscopy
items.caption_intent: Figure 5, Wittauer et al., Orthopaedic Surgery 2026;18:2247-2259; DOI 10.1111/os.70426; supplied PDF page 4. Fluoroscopic visualization of the partial ischial osteotomy in AP view (A): Medial (1) and lateral cortex (2) of the ischium; in iliac oblique view (B): posterior cortex (3) and anterior cortex (4) of the ischium. The starting point of the ischial osteotomy is distal to the joint (5) in the subcotyloid groove.

items.teaching_point_placement: Medial retroacetabular cut connecting with the ischial cut
items.caption_intent: Figure 8, Wittauer et al., Orthopaedic Surgery 2026;18:2247-2259; DOI 10.1111/os.70426; supplied PDF page 5. Illustration of the medial component of the retro- acetabular osteotomy with the hip in flexion. A straight osteotome is used for the initial portion of the osteotomy (4a) until it reaches the pel - vic brim, after which it is exchanged for an angled osteotome to com - plete the cut and connect with the partial ischial osteotomy (4b).
